title: Probabilistic semantics from a deterministic path
statement: Let a nondeterministic register program, oracle, input, guard, starting configuration $a$, reached state $l'$, register valuation $v'$, and rational $p$ be given. Suppose there is a finite run of the program with each choice resolved as false that starts at $a$, reaches $(l',v',	ext{no answer})$, and satisfies the guard at every configuration before reaching it. If $(l',v',	ext{no answer})$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $p$, then $a$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $p$.
hypotheses_covered: There is a deterministic reachability path from $a$ to $(l',v',\text{no answer})$ using the program with choices resolved as false
The guard holds at every configuration along that path before its endpoint
The reached configuration has probabilistic semantics with probability $p$
